title: okf-agent-memory
brief: Git-native persistent memory for AI coding agents — implements Google OKF v0.2 with sub-300µs in-memory BM25 search and an embedded MCP server. Claims to slash token bloat by 80%; that figure is the repo's and unverified.
caveat: Claims to slash token bloat by 80%; that figure is the repo's and unverified.
details: OKF Agent Memory (okf-memory/okf-agent-memory, 746 stars) is Git-native persistent memory for AI coding agents, implementing Google's Open Knowledge Format v0.2 in pure Go with zero dependencies. Its core idea is the Dual-Memory Agent Architecture: a tiny normative push layer (a ~100-150 token AGENTS.md codex in a compact "Agent Action Grammar") plus a semantic pull layer (an OKF knowledge bundle that costs 0 tokens at baseline, queried on demand). The pitch against the status quo: it avoids both the "prompt monolith" (stuffing everything into AGENTS.md) and the "RAG blindspot" (rules in vector DBs that agents never search for), claiming an 80% token reduction. Technical highlights: sub-300µs in-memory BM25 search, ~4ms graph validation, 4-tier memory scopes (project → vendor → user → system) with shadowing, provenance and trust tiers, search-before-write convention, code-to-knowledge binding, an embedded MCP server, and a registry for pulling vendor bundles. MIT.
